The history of the Roman Empire is a story of ambition, engineering, and administration. For centuries, Roman engineers built roads that connected distant provinces to the capital, and Roman law provided a framework that outlived the empire itself. Trade flourished along these roads, and goods from Egypt, Gaul, and Britain reached markets that had never seen them before. Yet the empire also faced serious problems. Corruption weakened the administration, civil wars drained the treasury, and pressure from migrating peoples tested the legions at every border. Historians still debate which of these factors mattered most, and whether the fall was sudden or gradual. What is clear is that the empire left a legacy of language, law, and infrastructure that shaped Europe for more than a thousand years.
